newsitem.title: SPAIN: Tabacalera first half results disappoint analysts.
newsitem.headline: Tabacalera first half results disappoint analysts.

text.p: Spain's Tabacalera group announced a 10.8 percent rise in first half net profit on Friday, disappointing some analysts' expectations as a summer cigarette price war cut into the tobacco group's results.
Tabacalera said first half group net profit was 7.133 billion pesetas ($56.9 million), up from 6.436 in the same period a year earlier.

One analyst said the company's disappointing results likely reflected provisioning for the second half to cope with the effects of a price war triggered in late July by a surprise government cigarette tax hike.

"I don't think (the results) are due to a fall in operating profits, but probably due to generic provisioning so that results don't alter significantly in the second half of the year," said Ramon Forcada, analyst at Ibersecurities.
The fledgling Spanish government, eager to cover a huge shortfall in the 1995 budget it discovered in late July, raised taxes on cigarettes and alcohol.
In response, Tabacalera raised prices on its black tobacco - whose major market is domestic.
But until now it has absorbed the price rise on Virginia, or blond, tobacco in an apparent attempt to maintain market share and sales in the highly competitive international field.
The implied impact on margins of either a fall in margin or a fall in sales has seen Tabacalera's share price decline to 5,120 pesetas now from around 6,600 pesetas on July 25.
According to Ibersecurities' Forcada, Tabacalera could have set aside 1.01 billion pesetas -- which appear under "variation in provisions" -- to offset expected weaker profits by year-end.
But a spokesman for Tabacalera told Reuters that this figure corresponds to provisions made for a downsizing plan, which has cost more than originally anticipated.
Sales figures for the first half were in line with forecasts.
"In sales there are no surprises. Results are in line with forecasts," said Carlos Ramos, of Ahorro Corporacion.
Group sales, net of value-added tax, rose to 354.2 billion pesetas, against forecasts for a rise to 369.5 billion pesetas.
